title: CRIT-7: Mark issues triaged with rodgers:triaged label
description:
Plan: plans/triage-workflow-plan.md §State Descriptions / NEW / UNCLASSIFIED

WHAT TO DO
Implement the triaged label marking logic that applies 'rodgers:triaged' label (or 'rodgers:triaged=true') to every issue processed by triage.

Create/modify files:
- src/triage/triage_loop.rs - Apply triaged label at end of processing each issue
- src/triage/mod.rs - Ensure label applied for all code paths

Behavior:
- Every issue processed by triage gets 'rodgers:triaged' label added
- Subsequent triage runs only process issues with rodgers:triaged=false (or missing)
- This enables idempotent triage - safe to re-run, same input = same result
- Label applied atomically with other triage labels

WHY
Without tracking which issues have been triaged, every run would reprocess all issues, wasting API calls and potentially causing duplicate actions. The triaged label enables incremental processing.

HOW TO VERIFY
- Unit test: Processed issue gets rodgers:triaged label
- Unit test: Second triage run skips already-triaged issues
- Unit test: Issues with rodgers:triaged=true not reprocessed
- Integration test: Hourly triage only processes new/changed issues
- Manual: Run triage twice, verify second run is fast (no work)

EDGE CASES AND PITFALLS
- Must apply label even if triage makes no other changes (issue was already correct)
- Label must be applied before any early returns/errors in triage
- GitHub API failure applying label should not fail entire triage run (log and continue)
- Bot issues get bot_labels then skipped - still mark triaged
- Label format: 'rodgers:triaged' (preferred) or 'rodgers:triaged=true'

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'rodgers:triaged': Label marking issue as processed by triage (idempotency key)
- 'Idempotent triage': Running triage multiple times produces same result
- 'Triage run': One scheduler tick processing all eligible issues
acceptance_criteria: Every issue processed by triage gets rodgers:triaged=true label (or rodgers:triaged label added) so subsequent runs only process new/changed issues - idempotent triage

title: CRIT-1: Triage runs on schedule and on issue events
description:
Plan: plans/triage-workflow-plan.md §Triage Loop

WHAT TO DO
Implement the triage scheduler that runs on two triggers:
1. Configurable cron schedule (default: hourly via scheduler.interval_minutes in config.yaml)
2. GitHub issue events: opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled

Create/modify files:
- src/triage/scheduler.rs - Scheduler implementation with cron and webhook event handling
- src/triage/mod.rs - Main triage loop entry point
- config.yaml - Add scheduler.interval_minutes configuration

WHY
The triage loop is the heartbeat of Rodgers. It must run regularly to process new issues and react to changes on existing issues. Without scheduled and event-driven runs, issues would sit untriaged indefinitely.

HOW TO VERIFY
- Unit test: scheduler triggers on cron interval
- Unit test: scheduler triggers on GitHub issue events (opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled)
- Integration test: Full triage run processes issues with rodgers:triaged=false
- Manual: Run 'rogers triage --once' and verify it processes un-triaged issues

EDGE CASES AND PITFALLS
- Must handle GitHub API rate limits gracefully with backoff
- Must be idempotent - processing same issue twice should not cause issues
- Must track last run timestamp to only process changed issues
- Webhook events may arrive out of order - handle gracefully
- Scheduler must not overlap runs - use locking if needed

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'rodgers:triaged' label: Custom label applied to issues after triage to mark them processed
- 'triage run': One complete pass of the triage loop over all eligible issues
acceptance_criteria: Triage workflow runs on configurable cron (default hourly) AND on GitHub issue events (opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled) - processes all open issues with rodgers:triaged=false

title: CRIT-1: Detect release candidacy from merged PRs since last tag
description:
Plan: plans/release-management-plan.md §Release Readiness / Criteria to Propose a Release (from main) → Acceptance Criteria CRIT-1

WHAT TO DO
Implement release candidacy detection that runs on schedule or manual trigger to find merged PRs since last release tag.

Create/modify files:
- src/release/detector.rs - Release candidacy detection logic
- src/release/mod.rs - Release manager entry point
- src/github/client.rs - GitHub API calls for merged PRs and tags

Detection logic:
- Query GitHub for merged PRs to main since last release tag (git describe --tags --abbrev=0)
- Group PRs by type using conventional commits: feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test
- Determine version bump: major for BREAKING CHANGE, minor for feat:, patch for fix:/others
- Only propose release if CI green on main and PRs exist since last tag

WHY
Automated release candidacy detection enables regular releases without human monitoring. Grouping by conventional commits enables semantic versioning and meaningful changelogs.

HOW TO VERIFY
- Unit test: Finds merged PRs since last tag
- Unit test: Groups PRs by conventional commit type correctly
- Unit test: Version bump calculation (BREAKING→major, feat→minor, fix→patch)
- Unit test: Skips if CI not green on main
- Integration test: Full detection run after merge to main
- Manual: Create test PRs, tag release, merge more PRs, run detector

EDGE CASES AND PITFALLS
- No tags exist yet (initial release) - handle gracefully
- Non-conventional commit PRs - categorize as chore or skip
- Multiple tags - use latest semver tag
- Release branches - detect separately per branch
- GitHub API pagination for many PRs
- Rate limiting on GitHub API calls

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'Release candidacy': Determination that a release should be proposed
- 'Conventional commits': Commit message format (feat:, fix:, BREAKING CHANGE:)
- 'Version bump': Semantic version increment (major/minor/patch)
- 'Last release tag': Most recent git tag matching v*.*.* pattern
acceptance_criteria: On schedule or manual trigger, Rodgers queries GitHub for merged PRs since last release tag, groups by type (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test), determines version bump (major/minor/patch) via conventional commits

title: CRIT-6: Config-driven question routing keywords
description:
Plan: plans/question-routing-plan.md §Configuration → Acceptance Criteria CRIT-6

WHAT TO DO
Implement config-driven question routing keywords for code search detection.

Create/modify files:
- src/config/schema.rs - Question routing config schema
- src/question_router/config.rs - Load routing keywords
- config.yaml - question_routing configuration section

Configuration keys:
- question_routing.code_search_keywords: List of keywords triggering code search
  Default: ['how does', 'what function', 'which module', 'internals', 'implementation', 'source code', 'walk me through', 'flow of', 'under the hood']
- question_routing.doc_search_path: Docs path to search (default: docs/)
- question_routing.code_search_path: Code path to search (default: **/*)

WHY
Config-driven keywords allow projects to customize what questions trigger code search without code changes. Different projects have different terminology.

HOW TO VERIFY
- Unit test: Config schema validates question_routing keys
- Unit test: Default keywords loaded when not specified
- Unit test: Custom keywords override defaults
- Unit test: Keywords used in code search detection
- Integration test: Question with custom keyword triggers code search
- Manual: Modify config.yaml, verify keywords loaded

EDGE CASES AND PITFALLS
- Empty keyword list - no code search triggered
- Case insensitive matching
- Keyword phrases (multi-word) - match as phrase
- Regex vs literal - use literal for simplicity
- rogers.yaml (repo-level) overrides config.yaml (host-level)
- Keywords also used in LLM prompt for classification

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'Code search keywords': Phrases that trigger source code search
- 'question_routing': Config section for question workflow
- 'Doc search path': Directory for documentation search
- 'Code search path': Glob pattern for code search
acceptance_criteria: Question routing keywords (how do i, how to, what is, why does, where can i find, explain, clarify, walk me through) are configurable in YAML, not hardcoded, with pattern matching and LLM fallback

description:

- Requestor rejects review - keep original, triage continues
- Requestor edits review comment - detect, ask again
- GitHub API failure on update - retry
- Large issue body - comment size limits
- Template field mapping: semantic not exact name match
- Partial template use - only fill missing fields

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'Reformatted content': Issue body rewritten with template structure
- 'Review comment': Reformatted version posted for approval
- 'Second approval': Confirmation to apply reformatted version
- 'Field mapping': Semantic mapping (environment→Environment, etc.)

description:

Implement strict enforcement: NEVER reformat issue without requestor's explicit approval.

- src/templates/mod.rs - Enforce approval requirement
- src/github/client.rs - post_comment, update_issue (with approval check)

Enforcement:
- Reformat offer posted (rogers-3wv)
- Wait for requestor affirmative reply
- Only on approval: reformat and update issue
- On decline: accept freeform, proceed with triage
- Key principle: 'Rodgers never reformats without explicit consent'

WHY
Requestor owns their issue. Reformatting without consent violates autonomy. Approval gate ensures requestor agrees to changes.

- Unit test: Reformat blocked without approval
- Unit test: Reformat proceeds with approval
- Unit test: Decline → freeform accepted, triage continues

- Approval detection: 'yes', 'please do', 'go ahead', 'looks good'
- Decline detection: 'no', 'don't', 'leave it', 'no thanks'
- Ambiguous response - ask for clarification
- GitHub API failure on update - retry, don't lose approval
- Requestor edits issue during wait - detect, restart
- Config reformat_consent=true (default, do not change)

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'Explicit approval': Clear affirmative from requestor
- 'Reformat': Rewrite issue body using template structure
- 'Freeform submission': Issue filed without template

title: AC-2: Config validation fails fast with descriptive errors
description:
Plan: plans/architecture-plan.md §Configuration / Configuration Schema → Acceptance Criteria AC-2

WHAT TO DO
Implement config validation that fails fast with descriptive errors.

Create/modify files:
- src/config/validation.rs - Validation logic

- config.yaml exists and valid YAML
- All required keys present

- github.token non-empty, not placeholder
- release.active_branches non-empty if releases configured

Error messages: descriptive, actionable, show missing/invalid key.

Fast failure with clear errors saves debugging time. Descriptive = actionable.

- Unit test: Missing required key → descriptive error

- Descriptive: key path, expected, actual
- Placeholder detection: common patterns
- Rodgers-required labels: 10 labels from architecture

- Env var expansion before validation

PROJECT-SPECIFIC TERMINOLOGY
- 'Fail fast': Stop immediately on validation error
- 'Descriptive errors': Key path, expected, actual, fix hint
- 'Placeholder token': YOUR_TOKEN, ghp_sample, etc.
- 'Rodgers-required labels': 10 workflow labels

title: Triage Workflow Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/triage-workflow-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: A new issue with a recognized template appears in the triage queue within one polling interval of creation
- [ ] CRIT-2: An issue missing a recognized template receives a single reformat offer comment within one polling interval; no repeat offers
- [ ] CRIT-3: A question issue receives an answer OR a doc-gap bead within one polling interval
- [ ] CRIT-4: A feature or bug issue transitions to ready-for-review only when all completeness requirements in plans/feature-bug-plan.md are satisfied
- [ ] CRIT-5: When an external user comments on a question issue, Rodgers re-evaluates the issue within one polling interval
- [ ] CRIT-6: Every triage evaluation is recorded in a bead (rodgers:type=triage) with issue number, decision, reason, and timestamp
- [ ] CRIT-7: Triage beads are append-only; they are never edited after creation
acceptance_criteria: Triage workflow fully implemented per plan

title: Release Management Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/release-management-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: After each successful merge to main, Rodgers computes next version (patch by default, minor for feat:, major for BREAKING CHANGE) using Conventional Commits
- [ ] CRIT-2: Rodgers creates an annotated Git tag matching computed version and pushes it to origin
- [ ] CRIT-3: Rodgers generates CHANGELOG.md entries grouped by type (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test) from conventional commits since last tag
- [ ] CRIT-4: Rodgers creates a GitHub Release with the tag, title 'Release vX.Y.Z', and generated changelog as release notes
- [ ] CRIT-5: On any failure (tag push, changelog write, release create), Rodgers files a bead with failure details and retries on next successful merge
- [ ] CRIT-6: All release operations happen in the bead context with audit trail
- [ ] CRIT-7: Release beads link to the merge commit that triggered them
acceptance_criteria: Release management fully implemented per plan

title: Question Routing Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/question-routing-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: When a question issue exists and docs exist that answer it, Rodgers posts a comment within one triage run with the correct doc link
- [ ] CRIT-2: When a question issue exists and no docs answer it, Rodgers searches the source code if the question is about implementation details before filing a doc-gap bead
- [ ] CRIT-3: When Rodgers finds an answer in the source code, it posts a plain-language explanation citing the relevant file, function, and line numbers, then closes the issue if fully answered
- [ ] CRIT-4: When a chore bead (rodgers:type=docs) is closed, Rodgers verifies the GitHub issue has a documentation link comment; if the link is missing, Rodgers posts it within one triage run; if the issue is already closed, Rodgers posts the link comment anyway; on GitHub API read failure, Rodgers retries on the next triage run without alerting
- [ ] CRIT-5: Rodgers never closes a question issue without either answering it or filing a chore bead (rodgers:type=docs)
- [ ] CRIT-6: Rodgers never routes a non-question issue through this workflow
acceptance_criteria: Question routing fully implemented per plan

title: Issue Templates Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/issue-templates-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: On startup, Rodgers detects whether .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ contains bug_report.md, feature_request.md, and question.md
- [ ] CRIT-2: When a project has no templates and auto_suggest: true, Rodgers files a bead with suggested default templates within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-3: A non-conforming issue (filed without template marker) receives a reformat offer comment within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-4: Rodgers never reformats an issue without the requestor's explicit approval
- [ ] CRIT-5: When a requestor approves a reformat, Rodgers posts the reformatted content as a comment for requestor review before applying it
- [ ] CRIT-6: All default template fields map to a completeness requirement in plans/feature-bug-plan.md or plans/question-routing-plan.md
- [ ] CRIT-7: A bug report with all required template fields populated transitions to ready-for-review without requesting additional information
acceptance_criteria: Issue templates fully implemented per plan
